text.scaleNote: Effort: 1 is under an hour and no money, 5 is a project with a budget. Impact: 1 is a nicer day for one person, 5 changes a KPI of the area.

statusHints.idea: Suggested, not yet looked at. Answer within a week.
statusHints.plan: Agreed what to try, who tries it and by when.
statusHints.do: Being tested, by the person who proposed it.
statusHints.act: The standard is changed and the result is verified.
statusHints.dropped: Not now, with a reason the person can read.

impact: 1 · a nicer day for one person
2 · one task easier for the team
3 · time or errors saved every day
4 · a KPI of the area moves

quadrantAdvice.Quick wins: Low effort, high impact: do it this week, with the person who had the idea.
quadrantAdvice.Projects: High effort, high impact: give it an owner, a budget and a plan, or take it to an A3.
quadrantAdvice.Fill-ins: Low effort, low impact: do it when there is slack, never ahead of a quick win.
quadrantAdvice.Thankless: High effort, low impact: drop it with thanks, or rethink it until the effort is small.

tips: Ten ideas that take an hour each beat one project that takes a year. Keep the bar low to enter and high to finish.
Every idea gets an answer within a week.
Plan it, test it or drop it with a reason the person can read. Ideas that wait teach people to stop having them.
The person who had the idea tests it.
They own the Do column. The leader removes what blocks them, not the idea.
Before and after: minutes, errors, metres walked. An idea without a measured check is an opinion.
Change the SOP, the shadow board or the training before the card moves to Adopted, or the old way comes back.
Quick wins first, projects on purpose.
Low effort and high impact goes this week. High effort and high impact gets a plan, a budget and an owner.
